subject: AtlasSupply: throughput cliff and error spike post qprofile v4.1 rollout
messages:
From: Cory Miller <cory.miller@atlassupply.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.com
Cc: Leah Wang <leah.wang@atlassupply.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden throughput drop + 5xx after your v4.1 qprofile swap

Alex —

We flipped to Redwood qprofile v4.1 in production at 02:30 AM PDT as planned. Within the hour we saw request throughput drop ~65% and a jump in 5xxs across our checkout inference routes. P99 latency climbed from ~180ms to ~760ms and error rates are still elevated. This has already impacted our peak traffic window — conversion is down and the ops team is flagging customer complaints.

Attached: service_logs_20270509.zip (trunc), and a brief CSV of error codes.

We need immediate mitigation. Can you confirm whether this qprofile change is behind the regression and what short-term rollback options exist? We need an ETA to restore prior behavior.

—Cory
CTO, AtlasSupply

Cory — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I’m escalating to our SRE/serving team now. Initial plan: Irene will validate whether v4.1 changed the serving kernel path or batching behavior for your model; Ben will prepare a rollback playbook we can run with you for an immediate mitigation.

Can you confirm: 1) whether you still have the old qprofile pinned on your side (so we can switch you back), and 2) whether you have a maintenance window this afternoon (PST) for a brief rollback if required.

Irene/Ben — placing the thread in your queues. I’ll loop in Marissa if we need exec attention.

—Alex

Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop + 5xx after your v4.1 qprofile swap

Alex / Cory — quick diagnostics from our side after ingesting the logs you sent (thanks Cory):

- Observation A: The v4.1 qprofile enables an aggressive KV-cache trimming behavior at shorter sequence breakpoints for the customer’s LLM variant. For AtlasSupply’s query length distribution, this caused cache churn and reduced effective batching.
- Observation B: We’re seeing an increase in decoded token retries in the serving runtime that manifest as transient 5xxs when the kernel falls back to a synchronous path under cache thrash.
- Observation C: The new kernel selection for v4.1 appears to route some requests to a fallback slower kernel on your primary pool due to an unexpected mismatch in sequence-length fingerprinting.

Immediate recommendations:
1) Roll back to qprofile v3.8 for AtlasSupply (this is the fastest mitigation).
2) Temporarily increase per-instance concurrency and enable an alternative kernel routing that preserves the older cache semantics (patch I’m preparing).

I’ve attached a short perf dump (perf_report_qprofile_v4.1.pdf) with traces. If you want a same-day rollback, Ben, can you outline the minimal steps to flip the profile?

—Irene
Sr. Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Cory Miller <cory.miller@atlassupply.com>, alex_martinez@redwood.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop + 5xx after your v4.1 qprofile swap

Cory — we can do a rollback within the hour if AtlasSupply can accept a short traffic flicker (~2–3 minutes) during the swap. Minimal rollback playbook (high level):

- Step 1: Pin AtlasSupply routes to qprofile v3.8 at the routing layer (no model change).
- Step 2: Warm the old profile on a small canary (10%) for 10 minutes, monitor p95/p99 and 5xxs.
- Step 3: If stable, broaden to 100% in a rolling fashion (switching shards) — expect 2–3 min of increased error risk while caches rehydrate.
- Step 4: Keep a temporary override that forces the legacy kernel selection for 2 hours while we iterate on a root cause fix.

I’ve put the concrete CLI commands in proposed_rollback_playbook.md (attached). Cory — do you want Redwood to execute steps 1–3 remotely, or would you prefer AtlasSupply to initiate the profile pin on your side?

—Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Also please preserve the service logs and traces for post-mortem — our compliance team may request them.

—Cory

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AtlasSupply: throughput cliff and error spike post qprofile v4.1 rollout

Summary / final status:
- Action taken: Ben executed the rollback to qprofile v3.8 at 11:12 AM PST on 2027-05-10 with a 10% canary, observed p99 drop from ~760ms to ~190ms and 5xx rate normalized within 12 minutes. Rolled to 100% at 11:26 AM PST.
- Current state: Throughput recovered to expected baselines; we’ve left a temporary legacy kernel override active for 2 hours. No additional customer-facing incidents reported after 11:40 AM.
- Next steps: Irene’s team will run a deterministic repro against AtlasSupply sequences to reproduce cache-churn and deliver a patch to v4.1 that preserves caching semantics. We will provide AtlasSupply with a root-cause write-up and the perf traces (link: https://drive.google.com/mocklink/atlassupply/perf-report) by EOD 2027-05-12.

Cory — apologies for the disruption. We’ll follow up with a post-mortem and a fix candidate before we reintroduce v4.1 to your environment.

—Alex
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
